description:
The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was launched by the Government of India on February 24, 2019. 

This initiative aims to provide financial support to small and marginal farmers across the country. 

The scheme was introduced in the backdrop of rising agrarian distress and the need for direct income support to farmers. 

The PM-KISAN scheme has been designed to alleviate the financial burden on farmers and ensure their economic stability. 

Under this scheme, eligible farmers receive an income support of ₹6,000 per year. 

This amount is disbursed in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each. 

The primary objective of PM-KISAN is to provide timely assistance to farmers for their agricultural needs. 

The scheme targets small and marginal farmers who own up to 2 hectares of cultivable land. 

As per the 2015-16 agricultural census, approximately 86% of farmers in India fall under the small and marginal category. 

The government aims to cover around 14 crore farmers under this scheme. 

The total financial outlay for the PM-KISAN scheme is estimated to be around ₹75,000 crore annually. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

To be eligible for the PM-KISAN scheme, farmers must meet certain criteria. 

Farmers must be landowners and possess cultivable land records. 

The scheme is applicable to all farmers irrespective of their caste, creed, or gender. 

However, certain categories of individuals are excluded from the scheme. 

These exclusions include institutional landholders, farmers who are in government service, and those who have retired from government service. 

Farmers who are in receipt of pension above ₹10,000 per month are also not eligible. 

To apply for the PM-KISAN scheme, farmers must follow a specific application process. 

The application can be submitted online through the PM-KISAN portal or offline through designated government offices. 

Farmers need to provide specific documents while applying for the scheme. 

These documents include land ownership records, Aadhaar card, and bank account details. 

The application process is designed to be user-friendly to ensure maximum participation. 

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes verification by the concerned authorities. 

The verification process ensures that only eligible beneficiaries receive the financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is done directly into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries. 

This direct benefit transfer mechanism helps in reducing leakages and ensuring transparency. 

The funds are typically disbursed in a staggered manner throughout the year. 

The government has committed to ensuring that the installments are released on time. 

The first installment is usually released in the month of April. 

Subsequent installments are released in August and December. 

The PM-KISAN scheme has seen significant uptake since its launch. 

As of October 2023, over 12 crore farmers have benefited from the scheme. 

The total amount disbursed under the scheme has crossed ₹1.5 lakh crore. 

The scheme has been instrumental in providing financial security to farmers during challenging times. 

It has also been a crucial support mechanism during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The government has made efforts to enhance awareness about the scheme. 

Various outreach programs have been conducted to educate farmers about the benefits of PM-KISAN. 

The scheme has been integrated with the e-KYC process to ensure authenticity. 

Farmers are encouraged to complete their e-KYC to continue receiving benefits. 

The PM-KISAN scheme is part of a broader strategy to improve the agricultural sector in India. 

It complements other initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and the Soil Health Card scheme. 

The government has also introduced a grievance redressal mechanism for beneficiaries. 

Farmers can lodge complaints related to their applications through the PM-KISAN portal. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the agricultural sector. 

Many farmers have reported an improvement in their financial conditions due to the assistance provided. 

The PM-KISAN scheme is seen as a step towards achieving the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The government has reiterated its commitment to supporting the agricultural community. 

The scheme has been extended and continues to evolve based on feedback from beneficiaries. 

In the fiscal year 2022-23, the government allocated ₹68,000 crore for the PM-KISAN scheme. 

This allocation reflects the government's focus on rural development and farmer welfare. 

The PM-KISAN scheme is a significant part of the government's efforts to enhance food security in India. 

It aims to empower farmers by providing them with the necessary financial resources. 

The scheme has also contributed to increasing the purchasing power of rural households. 

This has a positive impact on the overall rural economy. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of the PM-KISAN scheme. 

Regular assessments are conducted to ensure that the objectives are being met. 

The PM-KISAN scheme represents a critical intervention in the agricultural sector. 

It underscores the importance of direct income support for farmers in India. 

The scheme is expected to continue playing a vital role in the economic upliftment of farmers. 

The government remains committed to making necessary adjustments to enhance its effectiveness. 

Overall, the PM-KISAN scheme is a landmark initiative aimed at improving the livelihoods of millions of farmers in India.
